newsitem.title: COLUMBIA: Bomb blast rocks Colombian banana association.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast rocks Colombian banana association.

text.p: A bomb exploded outside the offices of a banana growers' association in an upscale district of the northwest city of Medellin on Tuesday, injuring at least 10 people, police said.
The blast was initially thought to have been caused by a car bomb but police said later the device, consisting of about 22 pounds (10 kg) of dynamite, was thrown from a passing motorcycle.

The bomb was directed at the offices of AUGURA, Colombia's main banana growers' association, based in the violence-torn northwest region of Uraba where leftist guerrillas and right-wing paramilitaries have killed with impunity for years.

"The bomb went off just after 9 a.m. (1500 GMT). It's terrible. Luckily nobody was killed but it damaged the building and injured workmates and some of the neighbours," an AUGURA employee, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters by telephone from Medellin.
"It appears the device was thrown by two people on a motorcycle. The package fell underneath a car and exploded, causing the 10 injuries," a police spokesman said.
One of the injured was said to be in serious condition, the Radionet radio network reported.
Provincial governor Alvaro Uribe immediately offered a reward of 100 million pesos ($100,000) for information leading to the arrest of the bombers.

Police said it was not immediately clear who was behind the explosion but leftist rebels operating in Uraba have accused growers and Sintrainagro, the main banana workers' union, of backing paramilitary groups -- charges they deny.

The heads of the main banana-growing companies with plantations in Uraba have been forced to leave the region because of fears of guerrilla attacks, mainly by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

Since 1989 more than 3,000 banana workers have been killed in rebel attacks. Most workers are linked to the Hope, Peace and Liberty political movement, which was set up after the Maoist-inspired rebels of the People's Liberation Army (EPL) laid down their arms under a government-backed peace plan.
Since then the FARC, seeing one of its former power bases depleted, has targeted the Sintrainagro union as well as the plantation bosses, represented by AUGURA.
